description:
What Are the Mysterious Bright Spots on Ceres?

Episode 80 of a daily journey through the universe. ✨
Ceres: the largest object in the asteroid belt, discovered on January 1, 1801, first called a planet, then an asteroid, now a dwarf planet. NASA's Dawn spacecraft revealed bright spots of salt in Occator Crater, left by salty water from below.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 81: Next stop, Psyche. A world that may be made of metal.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #ceres #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Why does a dwarf planet have glowing white spots? Scientists had to go and look.
On the first night of eighteen oh one, an Italian astronomer named Giuseppe Piazzi spotted a new point of light moving between Mars and Jupiter.
segments.headline: January 1, 1801

segments.text: It was called a planet. Then astronomers found many more objects nearby, and it was called an asteroid.
segments.headline: Planet? Asteroid?

segments.text: In two thousand six, it was named a dwarf planet, the same category as Pluto.
It's about nine hundred forty kilometers wide. The largest object in the asteroid belt.
In twenty fifteen, NASA's Dawn spacecraft arrived and spotted something strange: brilliant white spots in a crater called Occator.
segments.headline: Mysterious bright spots

segments.text: They turned out to be salt, left behind when salty water seeped up from below and evaporated.
segments.headline: They're salt

segments.text: Dawn found signs of a deep reservoir of salty water under the crust, maybe still partly liquid today.
segments.headline: Salty water below

segments.text: Dawn ran out of fuel in twenty eighteen. It's still orbiting Ceres, silent.
segments.headline: Dawn's last orbit

segments.text: Tomorrow, an asteroid that may be the exposed metal core of a baby planet. Next stop: Psyche. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
